scenario: [LDET.2.2b], [NLFC.8.1]: the other half of `freeing one leaves the other fully functional`. LDET.2.2b frees the source and drives the clone; this frees the CLONE and drives the source, so a clone that shared memory with its source in either direction fails one of the two. Same program, steps and comparison as LDET.2.2b: `fresh` emits a `logical` Fresh from `Ping p within 3_s`, behind a head-inserted `$ClockTick`, so the window reads the join candidate's entry stamp ([LTIM.2.8.6]). Pin: set 0; assert Ping a; pump; advance 1 s; pump; CLONE; then on both: assert Ping b; pump; advance 2.5 s, pump (Fresh a retracts); advance 1 s, pump (Fresh b retracts); FREE the clone; on the source: assert Ping c; pump (Fresh c). PATHS: libds `ds_engine_clone` and `ds_engine_free` through pyds `Engine.clone()` / `close()` (runner.py `_run_clone_determinism`); the Mercury runtime in test_behave.m's `run_clone_determinism`, where there is nothing to free and the vector holds it to its counts.
rules_ds:
schema Ping scope logical:
    k: String key

schema Fresh scope logical:
    k: String key

rule fresh:
    Ping p within 3_s
->
    emit Fresh logical k: p.k
